newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks down at noon on stock quota move.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks down at noon on stock quota move.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B shares were down at midday on Friday after the government announced a huge new stock issue quota of 30 billion yuan for 1997 to help cool down the markets, analysts said.
The foreign currency B share index lost 3.99 points or 2.31 percent to 168.54 points on turnover of HK$42.9 million.
The domestic currency A index ended the morning at 497.35 points, down 18.12 points or 3.51 percent, after free-falling 8.51 percent at the open. Turnover was 5.4 billion yuan.
"Prices plunged at the opening as investors scrambled to sell after the stock quota news, but I think they are regaining their composure," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Beijing said after the markets closed on Thursday that it would double the new stock issue quota to 30 billion yuan in 1997 from 15 billion in 1996.
Analysts said investors are now divided on the meaning of the move.
"The pessimists see this as a slap on the wrist," the analyst said. "Others hail this as a signal that the government is gaining confidence in China's markets."
"The indices are likely to fluctuate quickly, but in a narrow band this afternoon," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Analysts said the quota announcement was timed to be part of the government's recent anti-speculation drive that has spooked China's stock markets this week.
Rumours have swirled through the markets that several major brokerages may soon be banned from carrying out securities trading on their own accounts as a punishment for irregularities.
It has also been rumoured that the top securities regulator, China Securities Regulatory Commission chairman Zhou Daojiong, may be moved for failing to stop the markets from overheating.
China's stock indices have risen around 50 percent since the start of this year despite Beijing's repeated calls for the markets to cool down.
Officials at the CSRC have declined to comment.
In the B share market, Shenzhen Chiwan Petroleum Supply Base Co Ltd was the worst performer, plunging HK$0.37 or 8.81 percent to HK$3.83.
Pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd which on Thursday listed 100 million B shares, was the most heavily traded as 1.9 million shares changed hands. It lost HK$0.06 to end the morning at HK$5.83.
